source_question.stem: In a convex quadrilateral $PQRS$, $\angle P = 75^\circ$ and $\angle R = 105^\circ$. Which of the following statements provides the precise geometric criterion that guarantees vertices $P, Q, R,$ and $S$ are concyclic?

options.label: A
options.text: The adjacent angles are complementary: $\angle P + \angle Q = 90^\circ$.

options.label: B
options.text: The sum of a pair of opposite angles equals $180^\circ$: $\angle P + \angle R = 180^\circ$.

options.label: C
options.text: The opposite angles are equal: $\angle P = \angle R$.

options.label: D
options.text: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles.

answer.value: The sum of a pair of opposite angles equals 180

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: Recall the necessary and sufficient condition for four vertices of a quadrilateral to lie on a single circle.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: Compute the sum $\angle P + \angle R$ and relate this sum to the cyclic quadrilateral theorem.

distractor_rationales.opt-A: Student confuses concyclicity with complementary angles in a right triangle.
distractor_rationales.opt-C: Student confuses cyclic quadrilaterals with parallelograms where opposite angles are equal.
distractor_rationales.opt-D: Student confuses cyclic quadrilaterals with rhombi where diagonals are perpendicular.

core1a.title: Concyclicity and Cyclic Quadrilaterals
core1a.concept: A convex quadrilateral is concyclic (cyclic) if and only if each pair of opposite angles sums to 180 degrees. For angles alpha and beta, alpha + beta = 180 degrees ensures a circumcircle exists.
core1a.boundary_conditions: If opposite angles sum to strictly less than or greater than 180 degrees, the four vertices cannot lie on a common circle.

core1b.prediction_prompt: What relationship must opposite angles have for all four vertices to lie on a circle?
scaffold_steps: Recall inscribed angle theorem subtending semicircle or arc

html_representation:
In a convex quadrilateral $PQRS$, $\angle P = 75^\circ$ and $\angle R = 105^\circ$. Which of the following statements provides the precise geometric criterion that guarantees vertices $P, Q, R,$ and $S$ are concyclic?

Recall the necessary and sufficient condition for four vertices of a quadrilateral to lie on a single circle.

Compute the sum $\angle P + \angle R$ and relate this sum to the cyclic quadrilateral theorem.

Review Concyclicity Fundamentals
Show Complete Solution

By the converse of the cyclic quadrilateral theorem, if the sum of a pair of opposite angles of a convex quadrilateral is $180^\circ$, then the quadrilateral is cyclic (its four vertices are concyclic).

Here $\angle P + \angle R = 75^\circ + 105^\circ = 180^\circ$. Therefore, statement B is the exact criterion.
